summary: Eekedor's counting houses: the merchant council, loans and the exchange, the Compact's partner, the Arbitration Court and ledgers at war.

merchant_council.name: The Council of Merchant Houses
merchant_council.desc: Eekedor is ruled by a council of merchant houses that elects a Speaker every four years. The last election was held in 4A 1745, and nobody has yet found a reason to hold another.

merchant_council_2.name: Open Ledgers
merchant_council_2.desc: The ledgers of the houses are open to the council and to anyone who asks. A house that cheats is found out in a season, and a house that does not is trusted for a generation.

counting_houses.name: The Counting Houses
counting_houses.desc: Eekedor's counting houses lend to Sonargur, to the Compact and quietly, to the merchants of Parim. They trade in trust, and their ledgers have never been burnt.

counting_houses_2.name: Wealth of the East Shore
counting_houses_2.desc: The east shore is the richest strip of coast in the North. Its bills are accepted in every port of the Middle Lands and many beyond.

cargo_insurance.name: Insurance for Cargoes
cargo_insurance.desc: For a small fee, the houses of Eekedor guarantee a cargo against storm, wreck and theft. Shippers pay it gladly, and sleep better.

compact_tariffs_spirit.name: Compact Tariffs
compact_tariffs_spirit.desc: The Compact members trade with one another at a reduced tariff, set by the Eekedor council. The merchants say that the Compact is worth joining for this alone.

partnership.name: The Partnership Sealed
partnership.desc: Eekedor and Lerendor have signed a partnership in full, with a seal on each page. The Compact holds firmer, and the houses of Eekedor hold the strings.

impartial_bench.name: An Impartial Bench
impartial_bench.desc: Eekedor's judges have a name for fairness, and the council has taken steps to deserve it. A merchant who lost his case in Eekedor leaves complaining of the law, not of the judge.

law_merchant.name: The Law Merchant
law_merchant.desc: A code of trade, written by the bench and sworn to by the houses, covers every kind of contract. Merchants of a dozen realms quote it, and many have copied it.

war_ledgers.name: Ledgers at War
war_ledgers.desc: The houses keep a second set of books for the war, with columns for loans, escorts and losses. Eekedor's money works harder in a war than in peace.

neutral_houses.name: Neutral Counting Houses
neutral_houses.desc: The counting houses lend to all sides and favour none. A cargo insured in Eekedor is safe on any sea, and a debt owed to Eekedor is honoured by any flag.

a_gift_for_the_houses.title: A Gift for the Houses
a_gift_for_the_houses.desc: The almoners of the Houses of the First Light ask the counting houses to fund a hall of healing on the east shore. It would tend the poor, keep a granary and register every birth in the council's own ledger. The houses are generous with loans, and rather less so with gifts.

options.name: Charity is a matter for each house

eekedor_loan.title: A Loan from Eekedor
eekedor_loan.desc: A banker of Eekedor has been shown into the court at Sonargur, with a strongbox and a bill of exchange. The council offers the crown a loan at a modest rate, repayable over ten years. The terms are reasonable, and the lender is a friend.

council_in_eekedor.title: The Compact Council in Eekedor
council_in_eekedor.desc: The Speaker of Eekedor has asked that the next meeting of the Compact Council be held in his city. The counting houses will pay for the hall, the feast and the hospitality, and the council will have a fine view of the harbour.

eekedor_offers_arbitration.title: Eekedor Offers Arbitration
eekedor_offers_arbitration.desc: A judge of Eekedor presents himself at the court in Parim, in a plain grey robe. The council of merchants, he says, would be glad to hear the quarrel over the strait toll in its court, and to give a ruling that both sides can accept.

focuses.name: The Council of Eekedor
focuses.desc: Eekedor is one rich state on the east shore, ruled by a council of merchant houses. Speaker Pertav Oirt wants the treaty to last, the toll to stay low and the ledgers to balance.

focuses.name: The Houses Vote
focuses.desc: Each of the merchant houses has a vote, weighted by its tax paid. The count is public, and the dispute over weights takes longer than the debate.

focuses.name: Chapels of the Counting Houses
focuses.desc: The almoners of the Houses of the First Light ask the counting houses to fund a hall of healing. The merchants are cautious with gifts, and fond of ledgers.

focuses.name: Open Ledgers
focuses.desc: The houses agree to open their ledgers to the council. A house that cheats is found out in a season, and a house that does not is trusted for a generation.

focuses.name: The Speaker's Chair
focuses.desc: The Speaker's chair is carved of a single block of oak, from the harbour pile that held up the first quay of Eekedor. It is plain, hard and very old.

focuses.name: A Realm of Ledgers
focuses.desc: The council of Eekedor writes its customs into a charter: every house has a voice, every contract has a witness and every debt has a date. The charter is read aloud once a year, and copies are sold at the door.

focuses.name: The Counting Houses
focuses.desc: The counting houses of Eekedor are tall and narrow, with a strongroom in the cellar and a ledger-clerk at every window. They lend to Sonargur, and quietly, to the merchants of Parim.

focuses.name: Bills of Exchange
focuses.desc: The houses of Eekedor issue bills drawn on one another, accepted in every harbour from the strait to the Aenoran coast. A merchant can travel with a purse of paper, and be paid in silver at the other end.

focuses.name: The Harbour Exchange
focuses.desc: A hall of columns is built beside the harbour for the daily trade in bills and cargoes. Traders cry their prices from the steps, and the harbour clerks note them down.

focuses.name: Loans to Sonargur
focuses.desc: Eekedor's houses lend to the crown at Sonargur, at a modest rate and over many years. The loans bind the crown to the Compact more tightly than any treaty.

focuses.name: Loans to Parim's Merchants
focuses.desc: The houses also lend, quietly, to the merchants of Parim. The Speaker knows it, the council knows it and Sonargur does not ask.

focuses.name: Insurance for Cargoes
focuses.desc: The houses guarantee a cargo against storm and wreck for a fee. A shipper who pays it sleeps easy, and a house that is wrong loses a great deal.

focuses.name: The Eekedor Mint
focuses.desc: The council opens a mint beside the harbour, and strikes a silver piece with the sign of the pillared exchange. It becomes the standard coin of the east shore.

focuses.name: Wealth of the East Shore
focuses.desc: The east shore of the North is the richest strip of coast in the world, or so its factors say. Eekedor's bills are accepted in every port, and its warehouses are full.

focuses.name: The Compact's Partner
focuses.desc: Eekedor is Lerendor's partner in the Leren Compact, and the Speaker takes pains to remind the crown of it. His envoys sit on the Compact's left hand, and pay for the dinner.

focuses.name: Compact Harbour Rights
focuses.desc: Ships of the Compact have the right to anchor in Eekedor's harbour, take fresh water and unload for a fixed fee. The harbour is widened to hold them.

focuses.name: The Eastern Flotilla
focuses.desc: Eekedor builds a flotilla of galleys for the eastern waters, and mans it with hired captains and a few young merchants. It is small, quick and well supplied.

focuses.name: Compact Tariffs
focuses.desc: The council sets a reduced tariff for Compact members, collected at the harbour and kept in a separate ledger. Merchants say that the Compact is worth joining for this alone.

focuses.name: The Compact Council in Eekedor
focuses.desc: The Speaker proposes that the Compact Council meet in Eekedor, at the houses' expense. The crown at Sonargur may sit at the head of the table, but the table is in Eekedor.

focuses.name: Merchant Sea-Guard
focuses.desc: The houses hire a sea-guard of sturdy sailors and old soldiers to guard their cargoes. They are paid well, they drill often and they know how to fight on a crowded deck.

focuses.name: The Partnership Sealed
focuses.desc: Eekedor and Lerendor put their seals to a partnership in full: shared harbours, shared tariffs and a shared table. The Speaker has what he wanted, and the crown has what it needs.

focuses.name: The Arbitration Court
focuses.desc: The merchants of Eekedor have a name for fairness, and the council proposes to use it. A court is opened in the harbour hall, with three judges and a seal.

focuses.name: An Impartial Bench
focuses.desc: The judges swear to hear every case without favour, and to rule against their own house if the law requires. The oath is public, and it is tested often.

focuses.name: Judges of the Strait
focuses.desc: The court makes the strait toll its first case, and sends a judge to Sonargur and another to Parim to take evidence. Neither crown is pleased, and neither can refuse.

focuses.name: The Law Merchant
focuses.desc: The bench writes a code of trade that covers contracts, debts, shipwrecks and bills of exchange. Merchants of a dozen realms quote it, and many have copied it.

focuses.name: Offer Arbitration
focuses.desc: The council offers to judge the toll quarrel between Lerendor and Parim. The strait's two masters have both accused each other, and neither has so far been willing to hear a third party.

focuses.name: The Court of the North
focuses.desc: The court becomes known across the North as the place where quarrels are settled. Embassies come to it, and merchants swear their contracts there.

focuses.name: Ledgers at War
focuses.desc: The houses open a second set of ledgers for the war, with columns for loans, escorts and losses. Eekedor's money works harder in a war than in peace.

focuses.name: War Loans
focuses.desc: The houses extend loans to the Compact's crowns at a reasonable rate. The money buys arms for the Long Watch, and Eekedor holds the bonds.

focuses.name: Escort the Compact
focuses.desc: Eekedor's galleys escort the Compact's merchant ships through the northern waters. Their captains are paid by the voyage and are very prompt.

focuses.name: Neutral Counting Houses
focuses.desc: Lerendor has left the old treaty, and Eekedor follows it out. The counting houses declare themselves neutral, and promise to lend to all sides alike.

focuses.name: Coin for the Coalition
focuses.desc: The Heir has returned, and the counting houses open their strongrooms. Silver and arms go to the coalition, because a debtor who wins is worth more than a creditor who loses.

focuses.name: The Ledgers Balance
focuses.desc: The war is over, the loans are repaid and the books are closed. The houses settle their accounts, and the Speaker reads the final sum aloud in the council hall.
